title: AIDD common definitions
description: Shared vocabulary for every AIDD object. Tokens are snake_case and English.

aidd_version.description: The aidd release this record conforms to; the method and the toolkit share one version.

identity.description: `@user`, `@org/team`, `agent:<name>`, `email:<address>`, or a platform login; any of them may be qualified with a tenant as `<tenant>:<identity>`.

tenant.description: A tenant id: the company, or an agency's client, that a repository and its approvers belong to. Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, 2 to 63 characters.

glob.description: Repo-relative path glob. `*` stays inside one segment, `**` spans segments, a trailing `/` matches a directory.

command.description: Command vector, one argument per item. Never a shell string.

date.description: Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD. The pattern rejects an impossible month or day (2026-13-01, 2026-04-31, 2026-02-30) with any validator; February 29 of a year that is not a leap year passes the pattern and fails only `format: date`, which aidd asserts but a stock validator may treat as an annotation.

route.description: How much control a change gets. The names follow ITIL change types.

x-meanings.standard: A pre-approved change class from config standard_changes, such as a bot's dependency patch. Merges on green tests with no human approval. Never touches protected paths.
x-meanings.minor: Small, reversible, one Task, no risk dimension, within the minor budget. No Spec file needed; one Merge approval.
x-meanings.normal: Everything that is not minor, standard, major, or emergency. Spec, Spec approval, SHA-bound tests with red-then-green, one Merge approval.
x-meanings.major: Touches a protected path, data, security, privacy, money, or compliance, or cannot be reverted. Normal plus a specialist review, an observe block, and stricter profile gates. Computed by the gate, never guessed.
x-meanings.emergency: Production is broken now and this change is the repair. Allowed under a freeze. Smoke tests still run; the Spec and the review follow by review_due.

lane.description: The steps a route runs. Derived from the route: fast for standard and minor, spec for normal and major, emergency for emergency.

x-meanings.fast: The default: Implement ⟲ Verify -> Review -> Ship for standard (no human approval) and minor (one Merge approval).
x-meanings.spec: Specify -> Spec approval -> Implement ⟲ Verify -> Review -> Merge approval -> Ship for normal and major changes, after an optional Plan.
x-meanings.emergency: Production repair: smoke tests and commander approval to ship, review and Spec follow.

type.description: What kind of change this is, in Conventional Commits vocabulary. `data`, `security`, and `compliance` are always major.

x-meanings.feat: New or changed behavior someone can see. Needs a new-behavior test on normal and major.
x-meanings.fix: Restores intended behavior. Needs a test that fails before the fix (red) and passes after (green).
x-meanings.refactor: Structure changes, behavior does not. Existing tests must stay green.
x-meanings.perf: Same behavior, different cost. Acceptance is a threshold.
x-meanings.docs: Documentation, content, or generated reference only.
x-meanings.build: Build system, packaging, or developer tooling.
x-meanings.ci: Continuous integration or delivery pipelines and agent configuration.
x-meanings.chore: Housekeeping that changes no behavior: formatting, renames, cleanup.
x-meanings.deps: Adds, removes, or upgrades a third-party package.
x-meanings.infra: Runtime, network, or deployment infrastructure, including infrastructure as code.
x-meanings.data: Schema, migration, backfill, or production data. Always major.
x-meanings.security: Identity, access, roles, secrets, or cryptography. Always major.
x-meanings.compliance: Driven by a legal or regulatory control. Always major.

status.description: Spec lifecycle status, optional bookkeeping: the gate derives the real state from the PR/MR.

x-meanings.draft: Being assessed or specified; nothing approved yet.
x-meanings.ready: Spec approval: a human approved the Spec hash. Implementation may start.
x-meanings.in_progress: Tasks are being implemented inside their scope, verified as they go.
x-meanings.in_review: Tests are green on head; the change waits for Merge approval.
x-meanings.released: Merged and deployed. The observe window runs now.
x-meanings.done: The observe window passed, or none was required. Terminal.
x-meanings.rolled_back: The rollback trigger fired, or a person rolled it back. Terminal; Learn follows.
x-meanings.cancelled: Stopped by a decision, a freeze, or a final reject. Terminal.

status_group.description: The group every status falls into, the same five for Specs, Epics, Initiatives, and proposals, so a board or a tracker can mirror any object by its group. `aidd next --json` gives each step's group. The gate never reads it.

x-meanings.backlog: Written down, not yet planned or approved: a draft, or a proposal still being qualified.
x-meanings.unstarted: Approved and ready; nobody has started it.
x-meanings.started: Open work: being built, waiting for a person, blocked, or watched after release.
x-meanings.completed: Finished: done, rolled back (the work ended and Learn follows), or a proposal the addressee accepted.
x-meanings.cancelled: Stopped without delivery: cancelled, rejected, withdrawn, or a no-go.

type.description: blocks: the other item waits for this one. blocked_by: this one waits for the other. duplicates: this one repeats the other, which carries the work, so `aidd next` treats this one as cancelled. relates_to: see also. implements: this one delivers the other.

id.description: The other Spec, Epic, or Initiative, by id, in the Specs folder.

relation.description: A typed link to another work item. `aidd validate` checks that the target exists and that `blocks` and `blocked_by` form no cycle; `aidd next` shows an item blocked_by unfinished work as blocked. Bookkeeping: the gate never reads it and the Spec approval hash ignores it. A Task's `depends_on`, which orders Tasks inside one Spec, is unrelated.

relations.description: Typed links to other Specs, Epics, or Initiatives: blocks, blocked_by, duplicates, relates_to, implements. Bookkeeping: the gate never reads them and the Spec approval hash ignores them.

labels.description: Up to 8 labels, lowercase letters, digits, `:` and `-`, such as `area:billing` or `customer-ask`, for filtering (`aidd next --all --label`). They never change the route or the gate, and the Spec approval hash ignores them.

confidence.description: Confidence in the assessment. `low` stops the run.

x-meanings.high: Every fact that could change the route is known. open_questions is empty.
x-meanings.medium: Some facts are missing, and none of them could change the route. List them; the gate does not act on medium.
x-meanings.low: A missing fact could change the route. Stop and ask.

dimension.description: Blast-radius dimension, in words any role uses. `data`, `security`, `privacy`, `financial`, and `compliance` force major and name the specialist pool that reviews; every dimension rules out minor. Irreversibility is `risk.reversible = false`, which also forces major.

x-meanings.data: Reads, writes, migrates, or deletes persistent or production data. Forces major; the `data` pool reviews.
x-meanings.security: Who can do what, and what can leak: authentication, authorization, roles, tokens, secrets, cryptography, attack surface. Forces major; the `security` pool reviews.
x-meanings.privacy: Personal data: collection, retention, sharing, deletion, consent. Forces major; the `privacy` pool reviews.
x-meanings.financial: Money moves or prices change: billing, payouts, pricing, ledgers, tax. Forces major; the `finance` pool reviews.
x-meanings.compliance: A legal, contractual, or regulatory control. Forces major; the `compliance` pool reviews.
x-meanings.availability: Can take a service down or degrade it: infrastructure, capacity, timeouts, limits. Rules out minor.
x-meanings.third_party: Adds or changes third-party code, services, images, or build inputs. Rules out minor.
x-meanings.cost: Can change spend materially: compute, storage, paid APIs, model tokens. Rules out minor.

pool.description: A specialist reviewer pool name in `owners.reviewers`, such as security, privacy, finance, compliance, or data.

profile.description: Conformance profile. Each one is stricter than the one before.

open_questions.description: Facts still unknown at assessment. Empty when confidence is high.

summary.description: Blast radius in one or two sentences: who or what changes behavior.

dimensions.description: Every dimension the change touches. Empty means none.

reversible.description: False when a revert does not restore the prior state, such as a destructive migration or an external side effect. False forces major.

risk.description: Blast radius: what changes, which dimensions it touches, and whether a revert restores the prior state.

new_behavior.description: True when this command proves new or fixed behavior. It must fail on the base commit (red) and pass on head (green).

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock limit. A timeout is a fail. Default 1800.

when_changed.description: Run and require this command only when a changed path matches. Omit to run it on every change.

covers.description: In a Spec: the Acceptance items this command proves, by id (`A1`, `A2`, ...). Optional; once any command declares it, `aidd validate` warns about an Acceptance item no command covers, and about an id the Acceptance section does not have. The gate never reads it.

test_command.description: One test command. Exit 0 is the only pass.

files.description: The test files, and the configuration they run through. Frozen by the Spec approval hash and never inside a Task's scope.

commands.description: Commands the runner executes. Exit 0 is the only pass.

tests.description: How the change is proven: the test files and the commands that run them.

commander.description: The incident commander, a human. Named before the repair starts.

review_due.description: Date the postmortem and the Spec backfill are due. The config sets the SLA.

emergency.description: The incident an emergency change repairs. Required on the emergency route.

signals.description: Dashboards, SLOs, or queries a human watches.

window.description: How long to watch, such as 30m, 24h, or 7d.

rollback_trigger.description: The condition that starts the rollback.

observe.description: What to watch after release, for how long, and when to roll back.

repo_path.description: A plain repo-relative file path: no leading `./` or `/`, no backslashes, no wildcards.

assisted_by.description: `harness/model` for each AI agent that wrote code or tests. Empty when only humans did.

sha.description: A 40- or 64-character lowercase hex git object ID.

identity.description: Who approved, as the repository's config names them.

at.description: When the approval was given (RFC 3339), from the platform; null when it did not say.

commit.description: The commit the approval is bound to: the head for a Merge approval, the commit a Spec approval named (null when it named none).

decision.description: The verdict posted by the gate: pass may merge, pending waits, fail blocks, error on gate crash.

phase.description: green runs on head; red runs the head's tests against the base code.

goal.description: The measurable goal of an Epic or Initiative.
